title: Telegram Vanishes From Apple App Store, Then Quietly Returns Hours Later
excerpt: The messaging platform was briefly delisted worldwide with no explanation from Apple or Telegram, weeks after India's unprecedented ban over exam fraud.
body:
• Telegram disappeared from Apple's App Store on Monday with no explanation, showing a "page can't be found" error for users worldwide.
  • The app was restored within hours, with Telegram confirming it "should soon be available again for all users" but offering no explanation for the removal.
  • Apple did not respond to requests for comment, leaving the cause of the delisting unclear.
  • The incident comes weeks after India temporarily banned Telegram over NEET exam fraud concerns, highlighting the platform's fraught relationship with regulators globally.

Gone and Back

Telegram's listing on Apple's App Store vanished on Monday, with users around the world encountering a message that read, "The page you're looking for can't be found." The disappearance affected search results and direct links to the app page, though existing installations continued to function.

https://x.com/SmedCharger/status/2084485257873473700

Within hours, the app was back. "Telegram has been restored on the App Store and should soon be available again for all users," the company said in a statement reported by Reuters, without elaborating on what caused the removal.

""Telegram has been restored on the App Store and should soon be available again for all users," the company said in a statement reported by Reuters, without elaborating on what caused the removal."

Apple did not respond to requests for comment made outside regular business hours. The brief delisting also affected Telegram's visibility in South Korea's App Store, where users reported the app disappearing from search results.

India's Shadow Over Telegram

The unexplained removal arrived against a backdrop of escalating regulatory pressure on the platform — particularly from India, Telegram's largest market with more than 150 million users.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PJHZK71jzA8

In June, the Indian government imposed an unprecedented blanket ban on Telegram, ordering internet service providers and app stores to block the platform until June 22. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology cited the circulation of leaked and fake NEET examination papers on Telegram channels, along with fraudulent offers promising access to question papers.

Telegram challenged the ban in the Delhi High Court, but the court ruled the restrictions were "lawful, proportionate and necessary" to protect the integrity of a national medical entrance examination. One signal from a source indicated Monday's App Store removal may have been connected to an India-driven delisting, though neither Apple nor Telegram confirmed this.

A Pattern of Platform Friction

Telegram's relationship with app store gatekeepers has grown increasingly fraught. Apple has previously removed or threatened to remove the app over content moderation concerns. The platform's founder, Pavel Durov, was arrested in France in 2024 over allegations that Telegram failed to adequately moderate illegal content, including child sexual abuse material. Durov was later released on bail, but the incident underscored the regulatory scrutiny facing the platform.

During India's June ban, Google removed Telegram from the Play Store within hours of the government order, while Apple initially kept the app available — only to delist it after the ban's formal implementation. The platform was restored on both stores after the ban expired.

What It Means

For Telegram's massive Indian user base — and the broader global community that relies on the platform for encrypted messaging, channels, and group communication — the brief disappearance is a reminder of how quickly access to a digital service can be disrupted. Whether Monday's removal was a technical glitch, a content moderation action, or a regulatory compliance measure remains unclear. Neither Telegram nor Apple has shown any appetite for explaining what happened.
